subject.title: [Feature]: Add optional capability descriptors to tool definitions

question: What canonical tool-capability descriptor taxonomy and trust semantics should OpenClaw expose to plugin policy and audit consumers?
rationale: The change turns tool metadata into public security-policy input and overlaps multiple open capability, provenance, audit, and permissions proposals, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent SDK and Gateway contract.

options.title: Approve Unified Advisory Descriptor Contract
options.body: Define additive optional descriptors with unknown-by-default semantics and thread them through tools, metadata, inventory, Gateway, trusted policies, and before_tool_call while stating that declarations do not bypass host policy.

options.title: Fold Into Capability Permissions
options.body: Keep this blocked behind the broader default-deny capability-permission model so descriptors ship only with an enforceable grant system.

options.title: Limit To Security Matrix First
options.body: Use the Security Matrix audit model as the first canonical consumer and avoid a general public descriptor field until that vocabulary and runtime-fact path lands.

recommendation.title: Approve Unified Advisory Descriptor Contract
recommendation.body: Define additive optional descriptors with unknown-by-default semantics and thread them through tools, metadata, inventory, Gateway, trusted policies, and before_tool_call while stating that declarations do not bypass host policy.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the adjacent trusted policy and plugin tool metadata foundation this contract would extend.
